plain probe through CLIProxyAPI pinned to the Codex login (temporary alias probe/gpt-6.1-sol). Hit 2 of 3 at 2.5 minutes and 3 of 3 at 5 minutes, then misses at some later ages (0 of 3 at 1 h, 2 of 3 at 2 h). The published 0 means that there is no tested age through which every check hit, not that this route does not cache. Of the earlier runs of this model on this route, C1 (cpa-8.0.53, 2026-11-04, plain probe with a cache key) also checked from 2.5 minutes and missed at 5 and 7.5 minutes (2 and 1 of 3), X1 started at 5 minutes, and H1, H2 were made by other clients (coding tools, low reasoning, larger prompts), so this is not a comparison that shows a change. Three window requests of 921,500 tokens went to the same login one to two minutes before the priming, and the owner's own sessions use the login, so an effect of load at priming is not excluded. The missing session_id is not the cause: CLIProxyAPI copies prompt_cache_key into the upstream session id. A run that continues this one, primed about four hours later with no window request before it (branch campaign/logins-long, CL1), missed again; it is running and will be published together with this run. Served by build ngvoicu-local-e8d8d777 (process of 2026-11-16 18:48:58); its 2-hour checks ran at 14:27 UTC through build ngvoicu-local-a64b6855 (the owner restarted the proxy at 16:18:13 local), every earlier request through e8d8d777. The Codex login answered those checks: from the restart to 16:29:29 its request counter rose by exactly the 6 two-hour checks of LC1 and LC3 and the OpenAI API key by none, and the alias probe/... exists on that login only

known.basis: CLIProxyAPI places the cache markers on requests from Claude logins itself and asks Anthropic for the 1-hour cache.
A Claude API key gets Anthropic's default 5-minute cache; the 1-hour cache only when the client asks for it.
A Claude API key with the claude-code-cli fingerprint profile is treated like a login: CLIProxyAPI asks for the 1-hour cache.
